Right, here are the numbers going into the final day. Our leader has entered all five events this season and she has qualified for four finals, which is the best record on the tour. Her average total is fourteen point one. Second place has a slightly lower average, thirteen point six, but she has won two events, so she has more big results and less consistency. The gap between them is two hundred and forty points, which sounds like a lot and is not. One good heat closes it. Heat win percentage: seventy per cent for the leader, sixty-two for second.

People ask me how many events a junior should do in a year, and the honest answer is fewer than they think. I have coached kids who have entered twelve events in a season and have not improved at all, because they have spent all their time travelling and no time training. Four or five is plenty. What matters is not how many events you have entered, it is how much time you have spent in the water between them. I would rather see an average of six point five and a lot of training than one big result and nothing else.
